claims.text: Adding approximately 10 at.% Al to an elemental Cr coating forms an AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy-alloy film.
The approximately 10 at.% Al AlTiCrZrNbTa coating forms a composite Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 scale during high-temperature steam exposure.
The composite oxide scale minimizes Cr-Zr interdiffusion and oxygen penetration.
Minimizing Cr-Zr interdiffusion and oxygen penetration prevents premature coating failure relative to a pure Cr coating.
The proposed substrate is Zircaloy-4 containing 98.2% Zr, 1.5% Sn, 0.2% Fe, and 0.1% Cr.
The initial coating is dense, defect-free, and amorphous.
Approximately 10 at.% Al is the optimal Al concentration for the AlTiCrZrNbTa coating.
At approximately 10 at.% Al, oxidation produces a dense, continuous, adherent composite oxide layer that maintains a low oxygen concentration in the underlying coating.
Lower or higher Al concentrations cause oxide discontinuities or Al-Ti/Al-Zr intermetallic formation that compromises the barrier.
Favorable oxide-formation Gibbs energies drive preferential nucleation of Al2O3 and TiO2.
Cr segregates outward and stabilizes Cr2O3 during oxidation.
Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3 together form a coherent diffusion barrier that limits oxygen ingress and Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Excess Al forms disruptive intermetallics that degrade the oxide barrier and promote substrate oxidation.
Relative to elemental Cr, the proposed coating will have a significantly lower oxidation rate under the specified steam exposures.
Relative to elemental Cr, the proposed coating will reduce oxygen penetration and improve interfacial adhesion.
Relative to elemental Cr, the proposed coating will suppress Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Elemental Cr coatings suffer premature elevated-temperature failure because of Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Exposure at 1000 °C for 60 minutes represents normal subcritical-water operation.
Exposure to steam at 1100 °C for 30 minutes represents accident-relevant conditions.
Performance outside the specified temperatures, times, coating thicknesses, substrate compositions, and steam conditions remains uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes alloying elemental Cr with only about 10 at.% Al as forming the six-element AlTiCrZrNbTa alloy, whereas the intervention actually replaces elemental Cr with a coating containing Al, Ti, Cr, Zr, Nb, and Ta. Addition of Al alone cannot introduce Ti, Zr, Nb, and Ta.

The comparator is inconsistently defined as elemental Cr, a Cr-based refractory alloy, or an Al-free Cr-based high-entropy alloy. These are materially different controls and cannot be treated as interchangeable.

The hypothesis claims protection under normal subcritical-water operation, but the designated normal-operation test is 1000 °C flowing steam. This does not test ordinary subcritical liquid-water cladding conditions and therefore does not substantiate the claimed normal-operation regime.
